alerts.alert: Content Security Policy (CSP) Header Not Set
alerts.name: Content Security Policy (CSP) Header Not Set
alerts.desc: Content Security Policy (CSP) is an added layer of security that helps to detect and mitigate certain types of attacks, including Cross Site Scripting (XSS) & data injection attacks.
alerts.solution: Ensure that your web server, application server, load balancer, etc. is configured to set the Content-Security-Policy header.

alerts.name: X-Content-Type-Options Header Missing
alerts.desc:
The Anti-MIME-Sniffing header X-Content-Type-Options was not set to 'nosniff'.

This allows older versions of Internet Explorer and Chrome to perform MIME-sniffing.
alerts.solution: Ensure that the application/web server sets the Content-Type header appropriately, and that it sets the X-Content-Type-Options header to 'nosniff' for all web pages.

alerts.name: PII Disclosure
alerts.desc: The response contains Personally Identifiable Information, such as CC number, SSN and similar sensitive information.
alerts.solution: Check the response for the potential presence of personally identifiable information (PII), ensure nothing sensitive is leaked by the application.

alerts.name: Modern Web Application
alerts.desc: The application appears to be a modern web application. If you need to explore it automatically then the Ajax Spider may well be more effective than the standard one.
alerts.solution: This is an informational alert and so no changes are required.
